transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

It’s mostly my sleep. It’s gotten… pretty out of hand. For a while I’d sleep maybe two or three hours and then be up making plans, feeling like I could just get going. Now I’m awake before dawn, tense in my stomach, and I don’t feel rested at all.
Can you describe what it feels like when you're making plans while only sleeping a few hours? Do you feel an unusually high level of energy or an elevated mood during those times?

Yes… there’s definitely more energy than usual. It feels like some kind of engine running inside me. I can’t really sit still, so I’m up before sunrise calling people, reworking proposals, jumping from one thing to the next. It doesn’t feel normal, exactly.
Have you noticed yourself becoming much more active than usual in your daily tasks or projects, or felt restless and unable to slow down?

Yes. I mean… more than usual. It’s like there’s an engine in me, and sitting still feels almost impossible. I’ll be up before sunrise calling people, rewriting proposals, moving from one thing to another… I don’t really stop.
Have the people around you, like family or coworkers, noticed this change in your energy or activity level?

Yes. They noticed. I think it was hard not to. I was up so early, calling people, rewriting things, moving from one task to the next… like I couldn’t just sit quietly. Some of them said I seemed wound up.
During these periods of increased energy and activity, have you also felt unusually happy, excited, or even overly confident — more so than is typical for you?

Yes… I suppose so. For weeks I felt almost… brilliantly optimistic, like every problem was small and I could handle anything. But if someone questioned me, I’d get sharp with them. I felt like they were getting in the way, or trying to undermine me.
After feeling this way for a while, did you experience a time when you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yes… after that, things went very flat. I used to spend whole afternoons at the museum, or with my photography, cooking, playing bridge. Lately I just look at the camera or the table and… there’s nothing there. Just the effort of pretending I care.
